page: Microsoft Azure L8ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) and provides 8 dedicated virtual CPUs. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a generous memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering its resources entirely on CPU execution, memory capacity, and fast local input and output operations.

A primary characteristic of the L8ps_v5 is its direct-attached NVMe solid-state drive storage, featuring a local capacity of 1920 GB. This high-speed NVMe volume delivers direct physical media performance for latency-sensitive storage patterns without relying solely on remote network-attached disks. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external networking configurations for external routing. As an ARM64-based compute environment, execution requires software compiled specifically for the AArch64 ecosystem, lacking x86-specific vector extensions.

The combination of dedicated ARM compute cores, 64.0 GB of memory, and 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes the L8ps_v5 efficient for I/O-heavy database workloads. The balance of 8 GB RAM per core paired with high-throughput local scratch space allows large datasets to be indexed and queried with minimal storage bottlenecks. Typical operational workloads for this instance include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational databases, cache tiers, real-time log ingestion systems, and big data ETL pipelines.
